title: China's Bright Horizon
summary:
China's Bright Horizon
China's growing reliance on seaborne crude oil imports will set the tone of the tanker market for the coming decade. As shown in the chart below, the size of China's reported spot program has increased five‐fold over the past ten years; rising from an equivalent of 11 VLCCs in 2000 to one of more than 55 VLCCs last year. Chinese charterers have accounted for about 30% of reported VLCC spot fixture activity year‐to‐date, as compared with less than 5% a decade ago.

children.title: The Arabian Gulf and Beyond
children.summary: Second only to the United States in oil consumption, demand for transportation fuels from China's growing middle class has been a factor in worldwide crude oil demand for years. The International Energy Agency expects China's oil demand to continue expanding at a rate of 4.7% in 2010, reaching 8.9 million barrels per day.

children.title: Refining its Role
children.summary: Also likely to impact future trade routes are the Chinese government's efforts to discourage the import of refined petroleum products, most prominently by supporting rapid growth in China's domestic refining sector. The construction of large, complex refineries within China, some built in cooperation with foreign multinationals, has helped expand Chinese crude oil demand in recent years and this trend is expected to continue, as shown in the chart below.

children.title: Chart: Refinery Capacity Outlook ‐ China
children.summary: The stockpiling of crude oil and refined products in China has also played a role in supplying demand for ships throughout the market slowdown last year. While changes in Chinese inventories are thought to have contributed significantly to recent Chinese consumption, there remains a great deal of uncertainty regarding inventory practices in China.

children.title: The Expanding Chinese Fleet
children.summary: China's expanding middle class, strategic stockpiling, and complex refining capacity ensure that it will continue to be a large ship, crude oil story. Recent efforts to expand ship‐owning may ultimately lead to structural changes in the tanker market.
